assessment.nobel_worthiness: A highly consequential account of how trade and technology reshape local labour demand, employment and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson provide a coherent and identifiable core for the empirical and conceptual contribution.
assessment.maturity: The findings have been extensively developed, debated and applied across labour, trade and regional research.
uncertainties: The relative roles of import competition, automation and other concurrent local shocks remain difficult to separate in every setting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-run measurement of income and wealth concentration has changed the empirical basis for studying inequality and public policy.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are central to the construction and analysis of distributional series, with Zucman central to the offshore-wealth extension.
assessment.maturity: The research agenda has generated durable datasets, broad scholarly use and substantial reassessment of historical distributional change.
uncertainties: Measurement choices for wealth, capitalisation and tax-record coverage can materially affect some estimates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work made natural resources, biodiversity and intergenerational wealth central economic objects rather than external background conditions.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are clearly associated with foundational dynamic analysis of exhaustible resources, while Dasgupta has extended the broader inclusive-wealth agenda.
assessment.maturity: The contribution is long-standing and increasingly relevant to policy measurement and environmental-economic accounting.
uncertainties: The operational measurement of biodiversity and inclusive wealth remains incomplete and model-dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The analysis of organisational routines and evolutionary change offers a durable alternative framework for understanding innovation, firms and economic dynamism.
assessment.attribution: Winter is an unmistakable central contributor to the named contribution.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have influenced organisational economics, innovation studies and long-run accounts of technological change for decades.
uncertainties: The contribution's boundaries overlap with a wider evolutionary research programme and make complete attribution difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data have yielded a powerful new empirical description of intergenerational mobility and place-based opportunity.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman form a well-defined core of the data-building and empirical research programme.
assessment.maturity: The work has produced replicated methods, widely used public evidence and substantial policy and scholarly influence.
uncertainties: Observed mobility patterns do not by themselves establish which local interventions causally generate opportunity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The research established management practices as measurable sources of persistent productivity differences across firms and countries.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen are especially central, with Sadun an important contributor to the organisational-capital programme.
assessment.maturity: The evidence spans many countries and has connected firm-level practices to aggregate productivity and development.
uncertainties: The extent to which measured management practices are causes rather than proxies for complementary firm capabilities remains contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Modern work on agglomeration and urban spatial structure has greatly improved understanding of the geographic concentration of productivity and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Glaeser, Moretti and Duranton are central figures in the contribution, though the field has many major contributors.
assessment.maturity: A large theoretical and empirical literature has accumulated across cities, housing, labour markets and regional development.
uncertainties: Sorting, amenity differences and local policy make causal attribution of urban productivity effects challenging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This body of political-economy research clarified how political institutions and state capacity shape fiscal choices, development and long-run economic performance.
assessment.attribution: Besley, Persson and Tabellini each made identifiable foundational contributions to the integrated research agenda.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been influential across political economy, development and economic history for many years.
uncertainties: Institutional variables are difficult to isolate empirically from deeper historical and social determinants.
